P1.evidence: Setter notes acknowledged but not read back: 'I've got a few notes about you. Looks like you spoke to Kim on our team, and I've got those details, but I'm curious, man...' — the prospect had read those notes himself and raised their contents later, so there was real material to reflect and it went unused. Frame was two-part: 'really go deep and understand exactly what's going on with your fitness right now and what it is you're looking to accomplish', with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement asked and given. Opening question was the sharpest version of P1d in the batch: 'In your opinion, what would you say is the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?'

P2.evidence: Much the strongest P2 of the batch on the checks that ran, and the age, height and weight check still missed — all three were volunteered inside the prospect's own BMI tangent ('I'm 5'11", 200 pounds', 'I'm about to be 39') and none was asked. P2d is a model of the check: 'When you say your back is bad, what parts of your whole back?' → slipped discs; then mechanism, then 'is that causing you pain throughout the day or how is that showing up for you in your day-to-day?', then 'if you had to rate it, scale one to ten?' → 'A good six, seven', then trajectory, 'has that been getting worse?' → consistent, and duration of roughly 20 years. Diet was properly interrogated for the first time in this batch — 'what does that typically look like? Do you mostly eat at home?' — producing a full daily intake and calorie range. Training week and results both covered. General health conditions only part-credit: joints were followed up ('is there any joints in particular?') but the surgery was dropped the moment the prospect said 'nothing serious', and no medication, condition or clearance question was ever asked. No sleep, no daily energy.

P3.evidence: Strong on the surface layers and stalled at the bridge. The rep asked for the single priority ('of those three things, what's the one that's maybe the biggest priority?'), covered mobility, strength and muscle explicitly, and got concrete can't-do examples — picking up rocks at the house build and 'you used to try to go over there and pick that thing up and be no problem. Now I'm like, okay.' P3d ran twice and well: 'has anything changed for you which has got you basically on this call?' and then the fuller version, 'usually something that's really driving them... what's really driving you to do something you've never done before?' The answer that came back was thin ('I don't know, I'm a, I just never have been in shape like that'), and the rep accepted it. The children came from the prospect unprompted — 'I have two small kids and wanting to be able to be healthy for them' — so P3f only part-credits, and it was never driven through to marriage, identity or legacy. The reflect-back was a competent summary rather than the scripted tie-down: 'Sounds like the bigger reason you mentioned your kids, being able to play with them, with sports.'

P4.evidence: Cleanly run. 'Have you ever worked with somebody on the fitness side of things, like a personal trainer, coach, online coach, anything like that?' → 'Never', then the FitBod app and why it failed: 'I had to be in a gym, and I was just tired of going to the gym. I'm too busy.' The blocker was surfaced by direct question — 'is it part of the reason why you haven't been working out traditionally because of the back?' — and the prospect named it himself three separate times: 'I just don't know what to do. I have no idea what to do.' P4f is marked not applicable rather than missed because for this prospect the information genuinely is the problem; he has never trained, so the scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line would have been false.

P5.evidence: Absent for the fourth consecutive call, and the material here was the richest in the batch: a 38-year-old with unhealed discs at six or seven out of ten, visibly losing strength, with two children aged seven and nine and a stated longevity motive. Not one of the four questions ran. The only consequence-shaped move came after the objection had landed and was a rebuttal rather than a frame — 'a lot of people in this situation, they kind of use the reason they need to do it is the reason why they're not going to do it.' Delivered forty minutes earlier as P5, that thought is the whole call.

P6.evidence: The only call in this batch where both commitment questions ran, and ran before the price. Belief: 'How do you feel about it all? Do you feel like that would get you to your goals?' → 'Yeah, I'm sure it does.' All-in: when the prospect hedged with 'the majority of it's going to be whether I stick with it', the rep asked exactly the right follow-up — 'do you feel like there's any reason why you wouldn't stick with it?' → 'No, no. Like I said, once I put my mind in this category, it's going to be done.' He then reinforced it by checking schedule volatility. What fails is P6c: when hesitation surfaced after the number, the script requires returning to Phase 5, and instead the rep went to financing options and then invented a $1,200 thirty-day tier.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — 'assuming that we could figure out the investment, do you feel like that's something you want to do?' — so step one applies and was not achieved; no payment was requested at any point and no link was sent. The prospect also declined the improvised trial. Steps two to four are downstream of a payment that never happened. The rep ended by dispositioning the call himself: 'We'll just call it a no for now.'

objection_plays.detail: Trigger explicit and repeated ('That's pretty high', 'I'm a tight wad', '$6,000 to work out is, that's a big investment'). The rep ran the isolate move twice and well — 'aside from the money, do you feel like working with Trevor, going through that process, would work for you?' and then the sharper value-versus-capacity split, 'do you feel like it's worth, let's say 6K... or is it more about do I have that much money to put towards this?' Both answers came back clean: the process is fine, the money exists. From there the play stops. No 'you're not in a should-I place, you're in a how place', no permission-to-be-honest question, and no financial picture at all — no monthly surplus, no savings, no cards, no available credit, no investments. Arguably the open-wallet was not even the right instrument here, because the prospect had already stated he has the money; the blocker was willingness and decision speed, which the script has no path for.

Trigger explicit three times, including 'I don't make decisions on money very quickly' and 'let me have some time, if you don't mind'. Two moves ran in substance: the direction check ('are you leaning towards doing it, but figuring out how to make it work? Or are you leaning away?') and the blocker question ('what is the main thing that you are hung up on?'). Everything else was skipped — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?'. Against a prospect whose entire self-description is disciplined and consistent, the identity move was the obvious one and did not run.

Trigger explicit: 'I've to talk about that with my wife and kids to consider, having an emergency fund to consider.' No scripted move ran. The rep's instinct was decent — he removed pressure with 'if it's like your last 6K, it probably doesn't make sense to do it at all' — but he never asked the money-aside belief question about his wife, never asked what obstacles she would raise, never asked whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and out of pain, never separated needing input from asking permission, and never offered the deposit-with-refund fallback the play specifies.

The clearest missed play in the batch. The prospect said 'I've been screwed before, too' and 'I've been talking to a guy who I don't know on the internet' — and the playbook contains a move written for exactly those words: 'BURNED BEFORE: if you got hurt in a relationship once, do you never trust again?'. It did not run, nor did any other OE move. The rep answered the factual questions honestly and the prospect conceded trust ('Everything you said, I believe you'), so the outcome was fine, but the play was available and unused.

Competing capital commitment with no scripted play: 'we're building a house right now. It's a lot of money too', plus a stated need to preserve an emergency fund. The script's money play assumes the constraint is access to funds, not that the funds are already earmarked for a house under construction. The rep acknowledged it and moved on.

Clinical fit, the known gap in the script. A prospect with unhealed slipped discs at six to seven out of ten was told the programme would be 'freeing up all the joint pain' and given a load-progression target of eight additional kilos. There is no scripted path for establishing whether loaded ballistic training is appropriate, no clearance question anywhere in the process, and the intake questions that would surface it sit in a post-purchase onboarding form.

notes: The rep's best discovery call by a distance — a proper pain workup, a real diet question, and the only P6 in the batch that ran both commitment questions before the number — and it still lost, because Phase 5 never ran and there was nothing to fall back on when a self-described tight wad met a number he had no reference for. Two things to fix: run the consequence frame off the back injury and the two kids, and stop inventing commercial structures at the objection; the $1,200 trial was declined and cost credibility.
